name: Direct medial approach to the distal femur
region: medial distal thigh and distal femur
corridor: Posterior border of the adductor-magnus tendon with sartorius retracted posteriorly and vastus medialis anteriorly

positioning.text: Position supine on a radiolucent table with the knee freely flexed; flexion relaxes medial tissues and permits posterior retraction of sartorius.

setup.text: Review CT for the medial and posterior fracture extent, prepare vascular instruments when arterial injury is suspected, and ensure access for orthogonal fluoroscopy.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the adductor tubercle, adductor-magnus tendon, medial epicondyle, medial joint line, patella, and expected course of the long saphenous vein.

incision.text: Make a straight longitudinal incision along the posterior border of the adductor-magnus tendon beginning near the adductor tubercle and extend proximally as required.

superficial_interval.text: Identify the anterior edge of sartorius and, with the knee flexed, retract sartorius posteriorly to expose the adductor-magnus tendon.

deep_interval.text: Retract adductor magnus and its tendon posteriorly and vastus medialis anteriorly to reach the medial femur; remain directly on bone when developing any posterior extension.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, sartorial fascia, sartorius-adductor region, interval between adductor magnus and vastus medialis, then medial femoral periosteum and optional capsule.

structures_encountered.text: Sartorius, adductor-magnus tendon, vastus medialis, medial distal femur, capsule, and posterior popliteal space may be encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Popliteal artery and vein, tibial nerve, saphenous nerve and vein, medial genicular vessels, and articular cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The popliteal neurovascular bundle lies immediately posterior to the distal femur; posterior dissection must be blunt, controlled, and performed with direct anatomic awareness.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid blind or forceful posterior retraction of adductor magnus and avoid prolonged compression of the popliteal bundle or traction on saphenous structures.

exposure.text: Exposes medial distal-femoral fractures and permits limited posterior access, possible popliteal vascular exploration, and extension toward the posterior cruciate ligament.

limitations.text: Posterior joint-surface visualization through a medial capsulotomy is limited; posterior coronal fragments may require a more specific exposure.

extensions.text: Extend proximally along adductor magnus, develop the posterior plane bluntly for vascular access, or add a capsulotomy for limited articular inspection.

indications.text: Use for medial distal-femoral or medial Hoffa fractures, selected posterior access, and distal-femur fractures complicated by suspected arterial injury.

relative_contraindications.text: Choose a parapatellar exposure when broad anterior articular reconstruction is required and a dedicated posterior or fragment-specific route when posterior visualization would otherwise be blind.

implant_implications.text: Supports medial buttress or fragment-specific fixation; drill and screw trajectories directed posteriorly require guarded depth because of the adjacent popliteal bundle.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use AP, lateral, and condylar oblique views to verify medial reduction, posterior fragment position, implant containment, and screw length.

closure.text: Obtain meticulous hemostasis, repair any capsulotomy, allow the muscular interval to return anatomically, then close fascia, subcutaneous tissue, and skin in layers.

complications.text: Complications include popliteal neurovascular injury, saphenous neuropathy, hematoma, articular malreduction, stiffness, infection, nonunion, and symptomatic medial implants.

bailouts.text: If posterior control cannot be obtained safely, stop blind dissection and add a dedicated fragment-specific or posterior exposure with vascular assistance when indicated.

procedure_applications.condition: A medial condylar or medial Hoffa fragment needs direct medial reduction, limited posterior access, or associated popliteal vascular exploration

questions.question: What tendon guides the incision?
questions.answer: The adductor-magnus tendon at the adductor tubercle.

questions.question: What muscles are retracted to expose the femur?
questions.answer: Adductor magnus posteriorly and vastus medialis anteriorly.

questions.question: What is the major posterior danger?
questions.answer: The popliteal neurovascular bundle directly behind the distal femur.
